subject: POC success measurement playbook and next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@traction.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC success measurement playbook and next steps

Alex / Mei — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Below is a concise playbook capturing what we agreed on for the 4-week POC, the measurable success criteria, owners, and immediate next steps. Please flag anything you want adjusted.

High-level objective:
- Validate that TractionAI can serve your core summarization and QA flows at production throughput while meeting cost and quality targets so you can move to a Dedicated commit.

Success pillars & concrete KPIs (agreed):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency < 120ms; p99 (tail) < 350ms on 2048-token context for baseline traffic shape.
- Throughput: sustained 180-220 inference requests/sec for the two critical routes (summarize, answer) with 95% success rate (no token-generation errors).
- Cost/token: average billing cost target <= $0.0009/token for the POC configuration (we'll report both gross and net after batching).
- Quality: intent-accuracy >= 92% and top-1 answer correctness >= 88% on your seeded eval set (we'll run the harness described below).

POC timeline & milestones (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (prework, 3 days): infra checklist, network rules, baseline telemetry installed. (Owner: Ben)
- Week 1 (smoke): deploy model variant + quick smoke tests; baseline latency/throughput measurement day. (Owners: Ben + Alex)
- Week 2 (scale & tuning): ramp traffic to target throughput, enable batching & cache profiles, collect cost/time breakdowns. (Owners: Ben + Hannah)
- Week 3 (quality sweep): run evaluation harness, iterate prompt templates, quantization checks. (Owners: Karthik + Alex)
- Week 4 (acceptance): finalize measurements, decision readout. Acceptance = meet all four pillars or agree on compensating actions. (Owners: Hannah + Traction stake)

Evaluation method (brief):
- We'll run your seeded eval set (500-1,000 labeled cases) through the harness in isolated windows to measure quality. Intent-accuracy is defined as label match on intent classification; we will also provide confusion matrices and per-case traces. Latency/throughput will be measured under a replay traffic shape derived from your production traces.

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) We attach a draft POC KPI sheet (traction_poc_kpis.xlsx) and network requirements PDF. Please confirm dataset access and a single point of contact for infra.
2) Ben will share a short checklist to get VLAN and firewall access.
3) Book a 30-min kickoff to align ramp schedule — propose Thu 30 Sep 9am PT.

Attachments: traction_poc_kpis.xlsx (spreadsheet), network_requirements.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Hannah — this looks good and very thorough, thanks. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the kickoff:

- For the quality metric: when you say "intent-accuracy >= 92%" can you share the exact matching rules? Is this normalized string match, or judged by human raters? We prefer an automated scorer for speed but can add a small human spot-check.
- On the cost/token target: we need a breakdown by model variant (base vs quantized) so procurement can map it to budget.
- Can we shift the kickoff to Thu 30 Sep 11am PT? Mei will drive dataset access and will confirm the dataset size (expect ~800 labeled cases).

Also — Mei will need the eval harness repo or instructions to run locally. Can you attach or point to the runner?

Thanks,
Alex
CTO, TractionAI

Cc: Mei Lin <mei.lin@stratagen.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success measurement playbook and next steps

Alex — great notes. Quick replies inline and next-action items below.

- Quality matching rules: default automated scorer is a normalized token-level F1 for QA and a label-level exact match for intent. For intent-accuracy we will accept the automated scorer for the POC but will run a 5% human spot-check sample for parity and report both numbers. (Owner: Karthik)
- Cost breakdown: we'll produce three columns in the KPI sheet — base fp16, int8-quantized, and batched effective cost. That will help procurement map to budget scenarios. (Owner: Ben + Karthik)
- Eval harness: attaching a lightweight runner and README. It runs from a simple Docker image and can be executed against either Redwood hosted endpoints or your sandbox. We'll also add a small sample dataset and the scoring script. Attachment: traction_eval_runner.tar.gz (runner + README).

Kickoff: Thu 30 Sep 11:00 AM PT works for us — I've scheduled a 30-min kickoff and shared the calendar hold. Please confirm attendee list; Mei, can you own dataset sharing and provide S3 read credentials or a Drive link by EOD Wed?

Acceptance gate reminder: to avoid false negatives we agreed to two out-of-the-box compensations: 1) if a single KPI misses by <=3% we run a focused remediation sprint (2 business days) and re-measure, 2) if cost exceeds target but quality is materially higher (>4% delta), we will propose an adjusted committed pricing for your review. Any objections please flag now.

Next actions (owners & ETA):
- Hannah: finalize calendar invite and add acceptance gate language to KPI sheet (today).
- Ben: send VLAN/firewall checklist + confirm baseline test window (today EOD).
- Karthik: add automated scoring rules and cost-variant columns to attached KPI sheet (tomorrow).
- Mei/Alex: confirm dataset access method and point of contact (EOD Wed).

Thanks — see you Thu.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
(hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com)
